workouts.title: EE 0.1 Testing (Week 0, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Welcome to Day 1 of Endless Engine Testing! Although a 30-second sprint might not sound like much on paper, don’t be fooled—it’s going to challenge you. Be ready to push hard. Before getting started, make sure to watch these key videos: “What to Record” and “30sec Test Review.” Download the Endless Engine Score Sheet under the Files tab and use it to log your test results. This will help you track progress from Week 1 to Week 8 and set appropriate training paces for the rest of the program. Though we recommend keeping a personal training log to track your weekly workouts and jot down any helpful notes or takeaways.

workouts.title: EE 0.2 Testing (Week 0, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Welcome to Day 2 of our Endless Engine testing. Today we're going to measure your 2km time trial row. For this test, review this video to start, What to Record. If you haven’t already, download the Endless Engine Score Sheet under the Files tab and use it to log your test results. We also recommend keeping a personal training log to track your weekly workouts and jot down any helpful notes or takeaways. Ultimately, don't worry too much about "proper" damper settings, row technique or foot strap position - Just row how you normally would if this workout showed up in class. Strap in and go for gold!

items.movement: Record your final time and 500m splits
Use the preloaded 2000m option on the PM5 monitor for accurate splits and distance—no need to free row.

workouts.title: EE 0.3 Testing (Week 0, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Today, you’ll lace up and record your 5km run time. Whether it takes 15 or 75 minutes, the goal is steady, consistent effort from start to finish. Run at a manageable pace, and if you need to walk, that’s okay — just aim to add in bursts of jogging when you can. Before the run, review this video, What to Record. To measure your distance, use a tool like On the Go Map, Google Maps, or a GPS-based app like Strava, Adidas Running or Runkeeper, to name a few. Remember, 5 km is equal to 5000m or 3.106 miles. Don't forget to record your final run time and add the results to your Endless Engine Score Sheet under the Files tab.

workouts.title: EE 1.1 (Week 1, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Welcome to your first Air Bike workout. There are lots of sets today but push to stay consistent with your RPM's and calorie output. Remember, 10s is much shorter than 30s test so it should be possible to hit high numbers here. Take time to review proper set-up and technique in the Air Bike Academy and lay the ground work for solid mechanics! Use the Endless Engine Split Calculator to help you zero in on your pace times.

sections.name: AIR BIKE WORKOUT

items.movement: 10 sets x 10s @ 95-100% of your Max / Average RPM from last week's 30sec sprint test.
Record Max RPM + average RPM for every round.
Walk recovery | Record Max RPM + average RPM after each set

sections.notes: Work on the 2:00 mark. Once pace falls more than 25% take a longer break. When you can't keep up to the workout percentages, you're done for the day.

items.movement: Cool downs aid in recovery as they allow the body to get back to its baseline quicker.

workouts.title: EE 1.2 (Week 1, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Day 1 of Rowing!! We'll start honing our technique with the rowing drill warm-ups before each session but don't miss the videos in the Row Academy to help improve your technique and efficacy. Check out the Rowing 101: Rowing Overview before diving in today. Use the Endless Engine Split Calculator to help you zero in on your pace times.

items.movement: 6 Sets x 500m @ (~1-2s off our 500m split from our 2000m average)
Cool downs aid in recovery as they allow the body to get back to its baseline quicker.

workouts.title: EE 1.3 (Week 1, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Welcome to your first official Endless Engine run workout! Aim for a 85% interval running speed that should feel as fast but sustainable for the entire workout. Time and distance cover needs to be REPEATABLE for all the interval rounds programmed. Use the Endless Engine Split Calculator to help you zero in on your pace times.

items.movement: 10 minutes of 2 x 20 sec sprints @ 85% followed by 10 sec walks every minute.

Use a repeatable 30sec distance and aim for an 85% effort sprint. If 100% is as fast as you can possibly run today, pull it back to 85%. Which should be a pace you can maintain for the totality of the workout.
10 minute steady jog @ slower than 5k pace
Minute 1 • 20sec sprint @ 85% into 10 sec walk + 20sec sprint @ 85% into 10 sec walk
2 sprints every minute! A 20 sec sprint followed by a 10 sec rest walk before the next set.
Cool downs aid in recovery as they allow the body to get back to its baseline quicker.

workouts.title: EE 2.1 (Week 2, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Let's continue our Phosphagen energy system work on the Air Bike by increasing our to total sets to 12. Our mission is to stay consistent through all the sets and if possible, to build on our power output. Continue taking a rolling start if needed. You got this! Don’t forget you can use the Endless Engine Split Calculator to help you find your splits.

items.movement: Record Max RPM + average RPM for the entire workout
Once you fall off more than 25% of your workout RPM average the workout ends.
5-10 min additional light row or walk.

workouts.title: EE 2.2 (Week 2, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Focus on using the technique cues we've learned so far. For best results, film a few of your rowing sets and compare them to the Fault Fixer video. Don’t forget you can use the Endless Engine Split Calculator to help you find your splits.

sections.name: ROWING WORKOUT
sections.notes: Click here to see how to program the PM for this workout.

workouts.title: EE 2.3 (Week 2, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Today we're working a TOUGH consistent pace through 4 minute intervals. However, REPEATABILITY is the key goal so ensure we're covering the same distance for all 6 sets. Good luck! Don’t forget you can use the Endless Engine Split Calculator to help you find your splits.

items.movement: To review the full warm-up breakdown, check out EE 1.3.
Aim for 6 sets of 4 minute intervals at a TOUGH pace followed by a 2 min rest walk.
Goal is to cover the same distance each 4 minute interval.

workouts.title: EE 3.1 (Week 3, Workout 1)
workouts.description: We're up to 14 rounds this week with a 5 minute break between set 7 & 8. Want to know why? Watch the video above.

sections.name: AIR BIKE WORKOUT

items.movement: Record Max RPM + average RPM every round
Rest walk recovery to the 30:00 min mark.

sections.notes: Work on the 2:00 mark but note we take 5min break between minute 7 & 8. Once work falls off more than 25% of prescribed pace the workout ends.

items.movement: 5-10 min additional light bike or walk

workouts.title: EE 3.2 (Week 3, Workout 2)
workouts.description: If you're interested in learning more about why periodization is important, check out the video in the Engine Classroom.

items.movement: 6 Sets x 500m (start @ 2k Pace & faster 1sec/500m every round)

workouts.title: EE 3.3 (Week 3, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Let’s continue building our tempo and cadence by increasing our interval work to 15 minutes. Go by feel here, if Week 1 was challenging, ease up the pace slightly so you can sustain the full distance. Similarly, check in with yourself during the final 10-minute run. If you’ve got something left in the tank, see if you can match or exceed the distance you covered in Week 1. If not, settle into a comfortable, steady jog. Either way, you’re doing great.

items.movement: To review the full warm-up breakdown, check out EE 1.3.
Then, 15 minutes of 2x 20 sec sprints @85% followed by a 10sec walk.
Finish with 10 min easy, continuous jog.
10 min of steady jog @ faster than your 5k Pace
10 min easy, continuous jog @ slower than 5k pace

workouts.title: EE 4.1 (Week 4, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Whoa Nelly! Welcome to our longest Air Bike workout of the entire program. As we'll find out in later weeks, these long, challenging session aren't by accident. It's to cultivate something more important than just work capacity. Hint: 🧠💪 If you don't have an air bike that allows you to record max and average cals, just look at the screen and make your best educated guess on those numbers.

items.movement: Record Max RPM + average RPM for every set.
Work on the 2:00 mark but note we take 5min break between minute 8 & 9.
If you fall off more than 25% from your target RPM average the workout ends.
5 Min Break - Rest walk recovery to 19:00min
Rest walk recovery to 35:00 min mark.

workouts.title: EE 4.2 (Week 4, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Things are starting to get spicy! Today’s workout is 8 rounds of 500m rows. We’ll rest for 2 minutes between sets—except between rounds 4 and 5, when we’ll take a longer 4-minute break. Remember, you can always review your workout, times, and splits using the memory function on the ERG monitor. Ready to get more out of your row? Try a Quick Pull start—a series of short, powerful strokes—to get that fan wheel spinning and set the pace!

items.movement: 500m @ ~4 to 5 sec pace faster than 500m split time

workouts.title: EE 4.3 (Week 4, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Let’s continue building from Workout 2.3 with 5 rounds of 5-minute intervals at a TOUGH pace. If you don’t have a GPS smartwatch, use the out-and-back method to help ensure you’re hitting the same distance each round. The goal is repeatability and to be consistent across all sets.

items.movement: To review the full warm-up breakdown, check out EE 1.3.
5 sets of 5 min @TOUGH pace (ie. faster than 5k pace) followed by 2 minute walk.
Objective is to cover the same distance with each 5 minute interval.

workouts.title: EE 5.1 (Week 5, Workout 1)
workouts.description: We're graduating to 15 second sets of all out sprints. Go get 'em Tiger!

sections.name: AIR BIKE WORKOUT

items.movement: Record Max RPM + average RPM for every set.

workouts.title: EE 5.2 (Week 5, Workout 2)
workouts.description: A change-up today as we work through descending distance sets, focusing on finding a consistent rhythm and breaking through the catch. Before you start, be sure to review the module on breathing in the Engine Classroom.

items.movement: Descending meters (1000m/ 750m / 500m / 500m) while increasing 500m split speed.
Rest walk 3 minutes between each set

workouts.title: EE 5.3 (Week 5, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Forty sprints every 20 seconds might look daunting on paper, but the session moves quickly once you’re in it. Stay focused on the run mechanics we’ve been practicing, and remember—85% effort isn’t an all-out sprint. Aim for a consistent distance each round by staying steady and resisting the urge to come out too hot.

Finish with 10 min easy, continuous jog.
10 min of steady jog @ faster than your 5k Pace
Feeling fresh? Match your finishing pace from the 3.3 and continue working on being smooth and efficient.

workouts.title: EE 6.1 (Week 6, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Curious why the recovery is so much longer than the work time? It all comes down to how your body uses energy during high-intensity efforts. Want to learn more? Check out the Energy Systems module in the Endless Engine Classroom.

sections.name: AIR BIKE WORKOUT

items.movement: 12 total sets x 15 sec Air Bike @95-100%
Record Max RPM + average RPM for the entire workout

sections.notes: If you fall off more than 25% from your target RPM average the workout ends.

workouts.title: EE 6.2 (Week 6, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Pull those foot straps tight—today’s workout is 4 sets of 750m at 3 seconds faster than your 500m split from the 2k test. Aim for consistency across all sets. Dig deep. You’ve got this!

workouts.title: EE 6.3 (Week 6 Workout 3)
workouts.description: We’re adding a minute to our interval time this week, but the goal remains the same: Sustainable Speed. You should be running well below your 5K pace, and the work you put in today will pay off in spades in just a few weeks - So get after it! Let’s review what a @TOUGH pace really means: it’s a pace you can maintain for all rounds, but it’s definitely not easy. Most likely, it’s faster than your 5K pace, but it’s based on perceived effort. So ask yourself, what feels tough for you today?

items.movement: To review the full warm-up breakdown, check out EE 1.3.
5 rounds of 6 min @TOUGH pace run (ie. faster than 5k pace) followed by a 2 minute walk.
Aim to cover the same distance with each 6 minute interval.

workouts.title: EE 7.1 (Week 7, Workout 1)
workouts.description: This is our last Air Bike workout before the big Week 8 retest. Mentality is a huge part of engine work, and these long sets we’ve been building on each week are doing more than just boosting your conditioning—they’re building grit. If your bike doesn’t display RPMs, eyeball it as you go, or track your effort using wattage instead.

sections.name: AIR BIKE WORKOUT

items.movement: Record Max RPM + average RPM for the entire workout

sections.notes: Work every 2:00 but take a 5min rest between min 7 to 8. Once you fall off more than 25% from the target RPM the workout ends.

workouts.title: EE 7.2 (Week 7, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Pace, pace, pace! Engine work is all about pacing. Today, lock in your rhythm—focus on each stroke, settle in, and let the magic happen. If you fall off pace, don’t worry—adjust and rebuild. Take note: there’s a 5-minute rest between the 1000m and 750m intervals. Next week is our retest, so be sure to review the 2km Row Strategy video in the Row Academy.

workouts.title: EE 7.3 (Week 7 Workout 3)
workouts.description: It’s our final week of interval training! Just like in previous weeks, aim to cover the same distance each round at a pace noticeably faster than your 5K time—but remember, it’s all about perceived effort. That said, today is a perfect chance to test your pacing ahead of next week’s retest. Use it to dial in your effort and build confidence!

items.movement: To review the full warm-up breakdown, check out EE 1.3.
4 sets of 8 min running @TOUGH pace (ideally faster than 5k pace).
Aim to cover the same distance for each 8 minute interval.

workouts.title: EE 8.1 (Week 8 Workout 1)
workouts.description: Time to let all your Engine work shine! Be sure to review Coach Brandon's 30 sec Air Bike Test before doing the retest.

items.movement: Record Cals/ Distance & Wattage & compare to Week 1

workouts.title: EE 8.2 (Week 8 Workout 2)
workouts.description: You’ve done the work, refined your technique, built mental grit, and now it’s time to test your progress. Stay mentally present and stick to your 2km strategy. Make sure you’re well rested, and if you fall off pace, no problem—focus on finishing strong.

items.movement: Record your final time and 500m splits and compare to your first test in Week 0.
Again, Use the preloaded 2000m option on the PM5 monitor for accurate splits and distance.

workouts.title: EE 8.3 (Week 8 Workout 3)
workouts.description: Welcome to the final day of Engine Testing! Today, we lace up and race against the run time you set on the same course from Week 1. Aim for negative splits. Do not come out too hot—stay controlled at the start so you can finish strong. Best of luck! Don’t forget to complete the Endless Engine Completion Survey to unlock an additional 24 weeks of specific programming.
